newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Horn denies softening of economic policy.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Horn denies softening of economic policy.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Tuesday there would be no softening in the government's financial austerity programme despite political presssures to do so.
"This year, domestic consumption fell. Does this almost 10 percent fall show a softening?" Horn told journalists at a regular monthly news conference.

He said real wages also fell this year and living conditions have worsened in some respects, but the government would adhere as closely as possible to policies agreed with the International Monetary Fund.

Hungarian Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy had said on Saturday Hungary needed a strict 1997 budget and he was not satisfied with the pace of reforms to the social security system which accounts for a large part of Hungary's overall budget deficit.
Horn said reforms of the budget, the social security system and the educational system would take decades rather than years.
"We just made the first steps, but these steps cannot be unfounded as the society is not a guinea-pig," he added.
The Finance Ministry expects Hungary's social security deficit to run as high as 53 billion forints ($335.4 million) this year, compared with a target of 17.8 billion forints.
Horn said Hungary's 1997 budget will continue along the lines of stabilisation, but with lower tax burdens for the population and with measures aimed at encouraging enterprises.
Horn also said that in 1997 living conditions cannot deteriorate further.

He also gave his full backing to Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman, asked to resign by opposition party Young Democrats (FIDESZ-MPP) on Saturday following reports that the privatisation agency under his supervision paid consultancy fees considered exagerated.
"It is well known, that he (Suchman) is an honest and extremely hard-working man... My confidence in him is unbroken," Horn said.
The state privatisation agency APV Rt reportedly gave a 300 million forints consultancy fee to Marta Tocsik for negotiating with local authorities on APV's behalf.
Horn on Monday instructed the Government Supervision Office to investigate the consultancy contracts and report the results in time for the October 4 cabinet meeting.
